title: Route config: add quantization_profile_ref (default-preserving)
author: Benji Okafor
release_notes: Internal: route configuration supports optional quantization_profile_ref; defaults to baseline behavior when unset/"default".
description: Summary: This PR extends the route configuration schema to include an optional quantization_profile_ref field. When the field is unset (or explicitly set to "default"), behavior is unchanged and the serving stack will continue to use the baseline (non-profile) execution path. Motivation: The Quantization Profile Library workstream needs a control-plane surface area to opt in per route (and later by region/tier) without changing tenant defaults. This PR is intentionally limited to route config wiring + compatibility-safe defaults; policy evaluation and runtime application are handled in follow-up PRs. Design notes: - New field: quantization_profile_ref (string). Allowed values in this PR are: unset/null, "default", or a concrete profile ref string (format validation in control plane comes later). - Default behavior: treat unset and "default" identically; downstream resolution returns "disabled" state for profile application. - Backwards compatibility: Existing routes deserialize cleanly; API responses omit the field unless explicitly set (to avoid unexpected diffs for customers mirroring config). - Serialization: Both REST JSON and internal protobuf/struct tags updated. - Audit/change tracking: This PR adds explicit diff output for the new field in route config change logs, but does not introduce new audit event types yet. Migration: Adds a schema migration to persist the new field in route_config storage with a NULL default. Includes a safe backfill job that is a no-op (leaves NULL) and can be rolled forward/back without rewriting large tables. API docs: Added inline docs in the route config API structs (Go) describing semantics, default handling, and examples. Testing: - Unit tests for (1) decode/encode stability, (2) patch semantics (field clearing vs unset), and (3) default equivalence between unset and "default". - Golden tests updated for route config snapshots. Rollout plan: Ship behind existing server-side feature gate (RouteConfigQuantizationRefWrite) for write paths only; read paths are safe because the field is optional and omitted by default. Once policy engine guardrails are merged, we can enable writes for internal accounts + design partners.

conversation: Ethan Park (review): The default/omission behavior is key. Can we make sure responses omit quantization_profile_ref unless the user set it? This avoids noisy diffs for customers who sync config via IaC.
Benji Okafor (author): Yep. Updated serializer: when field is nil or "default" we omit in JSON responses. Added a golden test covering omission for both cases.
Mina Haddad (review): Patch semantics: how do we distinguish clearing the field vs leaving it unchanged? If a user sends an empty string, do we treat it as clear or invalid?

Benji Okafor (author): Treat empty string as invalid. Clearing is done via explicit patch op "clear" or setting value to "default". I added a test that empty string returns 400 with a message pointing to allowed values.

Jordan Lee (review): Re: determinism, I know compatibility checks are later, but we should avoid accepting arbitrary refs that could create hidden behavior changes once runtime support lands. Can we at least validate format (e.g., max len + allowed chars) now?
Benji Okafor (author): Added basic format validation (len <= 128, [A-Za-z0-9._:/-]). No allowlist yet; that comes with policy engine checks (ENG-5815).
Michael Nguyen (review): Migration looks fine. Please make sure the down migration is safe and doesn’t drop data unexpectedly if we roll back the app after some writes.

Benji Okafor (author): Good call. Updated down migration to keep column but ignore reads (documented) since dropping could lose data. Also gated writes behind RouteConfigQuantizationRefWrite flag so prod won’t write until we’re ready.
Naomi Feldman (review): RBAC/audit: Even if you’re not adding new event types, we need confidence that diffs are visible for change reviews. Can you include the new field in the route diff output?

Benji Okafor (author): Added to route_diff.go output and updated tests. This should show up in existing audit/change-history pipeline once the event emitter includes diffs (already does for route updates).
Ethan Park (approve): Approving with the omission behavior + patch semantics change. Please coordinate with policy engine PR so writes don’t get enabled prematurely.
Mina Haddad (approve): LGTM. Thanks for clarifying empty string behavior.
Jordan Lee (approve): LGTM. Format validation is enough for this layer.
Michael Nguyen (approve): Approved after migration tweak.
